## Highlights

**Ready for large notebooks and shared folders.** Labradorite stays quick with
thousands of notes, picks up changes from other programs while you write, keeps
every theme readable, and greets a new notebook with a short guide.

## New

- **Live outside changes:** while a tab is visible it checks every 3 seconds
  whether notes changed in another program or tab, then refreshes the list and
  reloads the open note. A note with unsaved edits is never replaced; saving
  still asks you to compare and choose.
- **Welcome note:** the first time Labradorite creates its default notebook, it
  adds **Welcome to Labradorite**, a one-page tour of the app. Folders you open
  yourself never get one, and a deleted welcome note does not come back.
- **Search in the header:** Search notes moved from the sidebar to the top bar,
  between the note name and the save state. On phones it gets its own row and
  its results stay visible above the notes drawer.
- **Tags expand inline:** All tags is a disclosure like the folders, with tag
  counts, the current filter and an All tags reset.

## Improved

- **Large notebooks:** with 5,000 notes the server answers a list refresh in
  about 0.05 s instead of 0.6 s and a search for a common word in 0.15 s
  instead of 0.5 s, and the sidebar draws in about half the time.
- **Contrast in all 14 themes:** muted text, links and accents, buttons, search
  highlights and focus rings now meet WCAG AA. Palettes are unchanged; where one
  of their text colors would fall short (most in Ayu Light, Catppuccin Latte and
  Nord), the app darkens or lightens just that text until it passes.
- **Start page:** a large plus button creates a note, and the logo is the
  transparent Labradorite mark. The sidebar's New note button is taller.
- **Cleaner header:** the separate focus button is gone; Focus mode stays in
  View, Quick open and Ctrl/⌘ Shift F. The Shift key hint is drawn as an icon,
  and icons line up with their labels.
- The browser app is now written in strict TypeScript. Nothing changes in how it
  works, but more mistakes are caught before a release.

## Upgrading

Stop the previous Labradorite process and replace the binary. Your vault,
themes, browser drafts and settings carry over, with no conversion.

## Downloads

One archive for **Linux amd64** holds `labradorite`, the README, the guide, the
license and third-party notices. Check it against `SHA256SUMS`.

[Full changelog: v0.8.1 → v0.9.0](https://github.com/eg36/Labradorite/compare/v0.8.1...v0.9.0)
